model_meta.description: Inferred concept model of a rolling-ball worm transmission and its ball circulation mechanism.

subsystems.description: Helical worm assembly that engages balls and contains their recirculation route; embodiments include worm part and peg part.

parts.description: Worm part carrying the helical path and recirculation port; in the described embodiment it contains the deflection boss, oblique hole, and entry fillet.
Peg part coupled concentrically to the worm part; its U-shaped helical channel continues from the oblique hole to form part of the recirculation path.
Boss at the recirculation port that stops balls on their helical trajectory and directs them into the oblique hole.
Hole in the worm part receiving balls from the deflection boss and continuing into the peg-part channel.
Fillet at the recirculation port that smoothens ball entry from the helical tooth into the hole.
U-shaped helical channel in the peg part, continued from the oblique hole as part of the ball recirculation path.

subsystems.description: Toothed gear coupled to the worm through rolling spherical balls; tooth gaps correspond to ball travel over an engagement cycle.
Plurality of spherical rolling elements moving cyclically through active, passive, and recirculation portions of the path.
Race constraining balls on the passive path and maintaining contact on the worm helix.

item_flows.name: Spherical ball circulation
item_flows.notes: Internal cyclic motion of the balls through active contact between worm and gear, passive travel on the worm outside gear teeth where present, and recirculation through the worm. The route can enter recirculation directly at the helix end without traversing the passive region.

item_flows.name: Rotary motion transfer
item_flows.notes: Worm rotation engages balls which in turn rotate the gear.

actions.name: Transfer rotary motion through rolling balls

steps.description: Worm rotation engages balls on the active path between worm and gear.
Active balls roll against gear teeth and transfer motion to the gear.

Balls leaving active engagement may continue along the passive worm path, where the outer race constrains them; depending on the path orientation, balls can instead enter recirculation without traversing the passive region.

At the helix end, the worm-part recirculation port's deflection boss forces balls into an oblique hole; a fillet smoothens entry, and the hole continues into the peg part's U-shaped helical channel for passage through the worm and return toward the helix.

actions.name: Accommodate ball travel at gear teeth

steps.description: Gear teeth have full thickness in the central plane and lesser thickness toward both sides, making the gap wider toward both sides; the gap corresponds to ball swept space over a full engagement cycle while minimizing backlash.

The double-profile gear-tooth gap has a circular side profile substantially corresponding to the ball diameter and center, contacting the ball at its side portions, and a second concave profile at the bottom that leaves clearance so the ball does not contact the bottom.
